program: Foundation portfolio: overdose rescue access and housing-stability morbidity

nutshell.headline: A whole Foundation gift is not an all-rental-assistance gift
nutshell.body: Central $100,000 gift: 10% overdose rescue access, 10% rental stability, 80% other portfolio and support costs retained with unquantified health. Allocations and marginal effects are explicit priors.
nutshell.whyItMayWork: Additional rescue access can delay death despite recurrent risk; additional housing stability may improve finite adult health.
nutshell.whyWeAreCautious: No verified marginal offer, Foundation-only branch ledger or local causal health study. Whole-gift costs and clinical effects cannot be inferred from historical service counts.
nutshell.recommendationBlocker: Obtain a funded-versus-unfunded work queue, public/partner displacement ledger, unique-client overlap data and measured outcomes before recommending a tranche.

programSection.body: Foundation social-service giving is distinct from Church giving. Audit consolidates Foundation, Church and property LLCs; consolidated expenses are not a Foundation marginal allocation ledger. Active HEAT services include Narcan and same-day MOUD access with public partners; Welcome Center connects clients to rental funding and workshops.

steps.title: Allocate the complete gift
steps.detail: Overdose rescue access 10%; Rental stability 10%; Meals and food access 22%; Family youth and child development 10%; Violence prevention and women support 5%; Other HEAT, HIV/HCV, treatment navigation 7%; Policy and community engagement 4%; Central administration, fundraising, safety and operations 28%; Other portfolio, property and affiliate support 4%. All are analyst priors.

steps.title: Add genuinely new care
steps.detail: Subtract replacement of existing funding through separate .4 OD and .5 housing additionality priors. Nominal offers still incur all costs.

steps.title: Credit finite disjoint health
steps.detail: Unique OD survival cohorts; one adult per housing household outside OD cohort; all shared harms retained.

programSection.boundary: All marginal allocations are analyst priors summing to one, not audited fractions. Remaining 80% of central gift retained in denominator and unquantified. Offers include branch costs; separately allocated corporate costs not charged again.

model.headline: Central whole-gift health is dominated by the conditional overdose pathway
model.body: OD survival difference compares recurrent-hazard trajectories. Housing morbidity uses .112 external stability risk difference × .5 transfer × .1 utility gap × finite discounted common-survival exposure. This is a new explicit bridge, not the old .072 QALY coefficient. Both expected caseloads count people alive at intervention start, already conditioning on pre-service survival; delay only discounts health, and mortality starts with care rather than gift date.

equation.label: Regional net QALYs
equation.expression: OD added people × finite survival gain × residence share + disjoint housing adults × finite morbidity gain × residence share − shared and independent harms

model.uncertaintyBoundary: 18 joint and one-way scenarios are not confidence intervals. Zero and negative health remain. Favorable jointly optimistic SF $30,692 is not a measured bargain or posterior expectation. Computational linearity is only illustrative near the $100,000 gift.
model.fundingBoundary: Unknown not zero. Government, SF ERAP, Season of Sharing, problem-solving services, SFAF subcontract and existing donor-funded stock belong in baseline. Proposed public contract not guaranteed new money. No current unfunded queue or executable gift tranche.

evidence.population: Foundation, controlled Church and two property LLCs
evidence.result: $30,766,602 total expenses; $10,826,230 contract revenue. Program $18,342,460; Church $1,922,106; administration $7,766,659; fundraising $2,735,377.
evidence.transfer: Not standalone Foundation cost allocation or September 2026 room. No audit percentage becomes a marginal benefit multiplier.

evidence.design: VA two-year Markov economic model using observational TFA comparison
evidence.population: Veterans enrolled in SSVF homelessness prevention
evidence.result: Model input .112 higher probability of stable housing at program exit. Model output .144 QALYs not imported.
evidence.transfer: One-year persistence, .5 transfer and .1 morbidity gap are priors. No mortality benefit or child multiplier.

evidence.design: Current HEAT activity plus external post-overdose cohorts
evidence.population: GLIDE service users; external cohorts differ in date, drugs and healthcare
evidence.result: Naloxone access exists; recurrent overdose and competing mortality require finite survival accounting.
evidence.transfer: No causal GLIDE rescue increment or unique people per donor dollar measured; reported rescues/doses do not equal permanent lives saved.

reservations: Unknown not zero. Government, SF ERAP, Season of Sharing, problem-solving services, SFAF subcontract and existing donor-funded stock belong in baseline. Proposed public contract not guaranteed new money. No current unfunded queue or executable gift tranche.

Associated funding envelope = full gift plus nominal offered service outside resource priors. Modeled resource cost removes donor-funded rent-transfer prior once. External resources are non-transfer staff/supplies/partner real costs not paid by donor; incurred per nominal offer, including replaced/deduplicated activity. No induced savings credited. Not a validated societal ledger: other transfers, housing service opportunity costs, in-kind and public displacement remain uncertain.
VA discharge-state probability is not proof of a constant one-year SF effect; local health utility is missing.
Overlap exclusion requires unique-person linkage across HEAT and housing. 90% disjoint is unverified.
Consolidated Church/property scope and high support costs prevent relabeling an old program budget as all-organization efficiency.
excludedBenefits: 80% central unquantified portfolio: meals, children/families, violence prevention, other HEAT, policy, operations and affiliate/property support
Separate Church health or spiritual-wellbeing claims
MOUD, HIV, HCV and other health endpoints already potentially within OD cohort; no stacked mortality credit
Housing mortality, children, caregiver spillovers, wealth and shelter/healthcare savings
Any housing health after two-year maximum or OD survival beyond finite horizon
Historical program-only $427,361 price as current unrestricted-gift outcome
